title: Animation Compression Quality Comparison Tool
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive animation compression quality comparison tool. The tool allows users to compare original keyframe animation data against multiple compression levels side-by-side, with real-time error metrics.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark background (#1a1a2e). Perspective camera at position (0, 2, 8) looking at origin.
- Soft ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Create THREE identical humanoid stick-figure rigs side by side at x=-3, x=0, x=3. Each rig consists of: a sphere head (radius 0.2), a box torso (0.4x0.6x0.2), two upper arms (0.1x0.4x0.1), two lower arms (0.1x0.35x0.1), two upper legs (0.1x0.45x0.1), two lower legs (0.1x0.4x0.1). Connect them with small joint spheres (radius 0.06). Color the left rig green (#00ff88, 'Original'), center rig yellow (#ffcc00, 'Medium Compression'), right rig red (#ff4466, 'High Compression').
- Each rig performs a procedural walk cycle animation using sine/cosine functions on joint rotations. The ORIGINAL (left) uses full floating-point precision keyframes sampled at 60fps equivalent. MEDIUM compression quantizes rotation values to 2 decimal places and samples at 30fps equivalent (interpolating between). HIGH compression quantizes to 1 decimal place and samples at 15fps equivalent.

ANIMATION SYSTEM:
- The walk cycle should animate: shoulder joints (swing arms), hip joints (swing legs), knee joints (bend during walk), and a slight torso bob.
- Original animation: shoulder swing = sin(time * 3) * 0.8, hip swing = sin(time * 3 + PI) * 0.6, knee bend = max(0, sin(time * 6)) * 0.7, torso bob = sin(time * 6) * 0.05.
- Medium compression: same formulas but round all rotation values to 2 decimal places, and step time in increments of 1/30s (lerp between steps).
- High compression: round to 1 decimal place, step time in increments of 1/15s (lerp between steps).
- Animation plays automatically on load. Provide a global playback speed multiplier (default 1.0).

ERROR METRICS (computed every frame):
- For each compressed rig, compute Mean Squared Error (MSE) of all joint rotations vs the original rig. Sum squared differences of every animated joint rotation, divide by joint count.
- Compute Max Absolute Error: the single largest absolute rotation difference across all joints.
- Compute a 'Compression Ratio' label: Original=1.0x, Medium=2.0x, High=4.0x (fixed labels representing keyframe reduction).
- Track cumulative error over time (running sum of per-frame MSE) for both compressed versions.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- PLAY/PAUSE button (DOM, id='btn-play-pause'): toggles animation. Shows 'Pause' when playing, 'Play' when paused.
- SPEED slider (DOM, id='slider-speed', range 0.1 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) with label showing current value (id='label-speed').
- RESET button (DOM, id='btn-reset'): resets animation time to 0, resets cumulative errors to 0, resets all joint rotations to rest pose.
- FOCUS MODE buttons (DOM): three buttons with ids 'btn-focus-original', 'btn-focus-medium', 'btn-focus-high'. Clicking one zooms the camera to center on that rig (animate camera.position.x to the rig's x, camera.position.z to 5). Clicking again or clicking another returns to default view (0, 2, 8).
- OVERLAY TOGGLE button (DOM, id='btn-overlay'): toggles overlay mode. When active, all three rigs move to x=0 and render semi-transparent (opacity 0.5) so they overlap for direct visual comparison. Toggle off returns them to original positions and full opacity.
- KEYBOARD: Space = play/pause, R = reset, 1/2/3 = focus original/medium/high, O = toggle overlay, Up/Down arrows = increase/decrease speed by 0.1.
- FRAME STEP: When paused, Left/Right arrow keys step animation backward/forward by one frame (1/60s).

HUD / UI:
- Top-left panel (id='hud-panel') showing: current time (2 decimal places), playback speed, play state.
- Bottom panel (id='metrics-panel') showing a table with columns: [Rig Name, MSE, Max Error, Cumulative MSE, Compression Ratio]. One row per compressed rig (Medium, High). Update every frame.
- Labels above each rig in 3D (using CSS2DRenderer or sprite text): 'Original (1.0x)', 'Medium (2.0x)', 'High (4.0x)'.

STATE MANAGEMENT - expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- isPlaying (boolean)
- animationTime (number, seconds, 4 decimal precision)
- playbackSpeed (number)
- mediumMSE (number, current frame MSE for medium rig)
- highMSE (number, current frame MSE for high rig)
- mediumMaxError (number, current frame max absolute error)
- highMaxError (number, current frame max absolute error)
- mediumCumulativeMSE (number, running total)
- highCumulativeMSE (number, running total)
- focusTarget (string: 'none'|'original'|'medium'|'high')
- overlayMode (boolean)
- cameraX (number, camera world x position)
- cameraZ (number, camera world z position)
- jointCount (number, total animated joints per rig)
- frameCount (number, total frames elapsed since last reset)
- mediumCompressionRatio (number, 2.0)
- highCompressionRatio (number, 4.0)
- rigPositions (array of 3 x-values for the three rigs)
- rigOpacity (number, current opacity of rigs, 1.0 or 0.5)

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Animation compression must faithfully quantize rotation values: medium to 2 decimal places with 30fps sampling, high to 1 decimal place with 15fps sampling. MSE must always be >= 0. High compression MSE must always be >= medium compression MSE (more compression = more error). Cumulative MSE must be monotonically non-decreasing. All rotation values must be NaN-free. Camera transitions must be smooth (not teleporting).
